source.text: הֵ֤ן עַבְדִּי֙ אֶתְמָךְ־בּ֔וֹ בְּחִירִ֖י רָצְתָ֣ה נַפְשִׁ֑י נָתַ֤תִּי רוּחִי֙ עָלָ֔יו מִשְׁפָּ֖ט לַגּוֹיִ֥ם יוֹצִֽיא׃

records.literal_gloss: Here! my servant, I support him; my chosen, it is pleased [with him], my soul; I have put my spirit on him; justice to [the] nations he will bring out.

en.L: See, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant, whom I hold up, \q {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} chosen one, [with whom] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} soul is pleased; \q I have set {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Spirit upon him; \q justice to the nations he will bring out.
en.B: Here is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant; I hold him up. \q He is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} chosen one, and I am well pleased with him. \q I have placed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Spirit on him, \q and he will carry justice out to the nations.
en.R: Look at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant. I give him strength. \q I have chosen him, and he makes {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} glad. \q I have put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Spirit on him, \q and he will bring justice out to all the nations.

es.L: He aquí {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo, a quien sostengo, \q {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} escogido, [en quien] {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} alma se complace; \q he puesto {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Espíritu sobre él; \q él sacará la justicia a las naciones.
es.B: Aquí está {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo; yo lo sostengo. \q Es {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} escogido, y en él me complazco. \q He puesto {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Espíritu sobre él, \q y él llevará la justicia a las naciones.
es.R: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}} a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo. Yo le doy fuerzas. \q Yo lo escogí, y él {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} llena de alegría. \q He puesto {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Espíritu sobre él, \q y él llevará la justicia a todas las naciones.

sw.L: Tazama, mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, ninayemshika, \q mteule {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, [ambaye] nafsi {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} inapendezwa [naye]; \q nimeweka Roho {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} juu yake; \q ataleta haki kwa mataifa.
sw.B: Huyu hapa mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}; ninamshikilia. \q Yeye ni mteule {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, nami ninapendezwa naye sana. \q Nimeweka Roho {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} juu yake, \q naye atawapelekea mataifa haki.
sw.R: Mtazameni mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}. Ninampa nguvu. \q Nimemchagua, naye ananifurahisha. \q Nimeweka Roho {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} juu yake, \q naye ataleta haki kwa mataifa yote.

decisions.choice: my servant: one whom God chooses and sends to bring justice to the nations, here not named
decisions.reason: In 41:8-9 the servant is Israel, the people (see the note at 41:8). Here the servant is not named and has a mission to the nations, and in 42:6 and 49:5-6 the servant is sent to Israel itself. Matthew 12:18-21 quotes 42:1-4 of Jesus, who heals quietly and tells people not to make him known. Isaiah 42:19 again calls blind and deaf Israel God's servant.

decisions.choice: justice: the right order God wills, set up for all peoples
decisions.reason: The word means a just decision or the right way of things that a ruler establishes. It recurs three times in these verses (1, 3, 4), so it is the heart of the servant's task. It is not limited to court verdicts.

decisions.choice: my chosen, in whom my soul delights: God's pleasure in the servant
decisions.reason: "My soul" here means "I myself". The voice from heaven at Jesus' baptism (Mark 1:11) echoes this line. The Septuagint (from memory; to be checked) names the servant here as Jacob and the chosen one as Israel.

decisions.choice: I hold him up; I give him strength
decisions.reason: The verb means to grasp and support. Balanced keeps the picture of holding up; Readable says what the support gives.

decisions.choice: siervo, escogido, Espíritu, justicia
decisions.reason: Matthew 12:18 quotes this verse; Spanish keeps its key words ("mi siervo", "mi Espíritu", "la justicia") so the quotation can be recognized, without copying the Greek-based wording. The servant takes no deity_pronoun span ("él").

decisions.choice: haki
decisions.reason: In 42:1-4 the word for justice is "haki" at every level, the word of Matthew 12:18-20, which quotes these lines; elsewhere it is "hukumu" at Literal. "Mtumishi wangu", "Roho wangu" and "mteule wangu" keep the key words of Matthew 12:18 without copying its wording, which follows the Greek.

source.text: לֹ֥א יִצְעַ֖ק וְלֹ֣א יִשָּׂ֑א וְלֹֽא־יַשְׁמִ֥יעַ בַּח֖וּץ קוֹלֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Not he will cry out, and not he will lift up, and not he will make heard in the street his voice.

en.L: He will not cry out, and he will not lift up [his voice], \q and he will not make his voice heard in the street.
en.B: He will not shout or make an uproar; \q he will not send his voice ringing through the streets.
en.R: He will not yell or shout. \q He will not raise his voice to be heard out in the streets.

es.L: No gritará, ni alzará [la voz], \q ni hará oír su voz en la calle.
es.B: No gritará ni armará alboroto; \q no hará resonar su voz por las calles.
es.R: No gritará ni dará voces. \q No alzará la voz para que lo oigan en las calles.

sw.L: Hatapiga kelele, wala hatainua [sauti yake], \q wala hataisikizisha sauti yake barabarani.
sw.B: Hatapaza sauti wala hatafanya ghasia; \q hataivumisha sauti yake katika njia za mji.
sw.R: Hatapiga makelele wala kupaza sauti. \q Hatapandisha sauti yake ili isikike barabarani.

decisions.choice: he will not cry out or lift up his voice: the servant works quietly
decisions.reason: The verb "lift up" has no object; "voice" at the end of the verse serves all three verbs. The servant does not draw a crowd by loud proclaiming, unlike a herald or a ruler making announcements in the public square. Matthew 12:16-19 connects this with Jesus telling those he healed not to make him known.

decisions.choice: lift up [his voice]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the object the Hebrew leaves to be understood from the end of the verse.

source.text: קָנֶ֤ה רָצוּץ֙ לֹ֣א יִשְׁבּ֔וֹר וּפִשְׁתָּ֥ה כֵהָ֖ה לֹ֣א יְכַבֶּ֑נָּה לֶאֱמֶ֖ת יוֹצִ֥יא מִשְׁפָּֽט׃

records.literal_gloss: A reed crushed not he will break, and a wick dim not he will quench it; to faithfulness he will bring out justice.

en.L: A crushed reed he will not break, \q and a dimly burning wick he will not put out; \q in faithfulness he will bring out justice.
en.B: He will not snap off a split reed \q or smother a wick that is barely burning; \q with faithfulness he will bring justice out.
en.R: He will not break off a reed that is already cracked. \q He will not put out the flame of a lamp that is almost gone. \q He will be faithful and bring justice.

es.L: La caña aplastada no quebrará, \q y la mecha que apenas arde no apagará; \q con fidelidad sacará la justicia.
es.B: No acabará de romper la caña rajada \q ni sofocará la mecha que apenas arde; \q con fidelidad llevará adelante la justicia.
es.R: No romperá una caña que ya está quebrada. \q No apagará la llama de una lámpara que está a punto de apagarse. \q Será fiel y traerá la justicia.

sw.L: Tete lililopondeka hatalivunja, \q na utambi unaofuka moshi hatauzima; \q kwa uaminifu ataleta haki.
sw.B: Hatalivunja tete lililopasuka, \q wala hatauzima utambi unaowaka kwa shida; \q kwa uaminifu ataleta haki.
sw.R: Hatavunja unyasi ambao tayari umepasuka. \q Hatazima mwali wa taa ambao unakaribia kuzimika. \q Atakuwa mwaminifu na kuleta haki.

decisions.choice: a crushed reed, a dim wick: people who are weak and nearly finished
decisions.reason: A cracked reed is easily snapped and a smoking wick easily put out. The servant does not finish off what is already failing. Verse 4 picks up the same two words for the servant himself.

decisions.choice: in faithfulness: reliably, in keeping with what is true
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean "faithfully" (how he works) or "according to truth" (justice that is true). Both say the justice he brings is sure and right.

decisions.choice: the flame of a lamp
decisions.reason: Readable explains that the wick is the burning part of an oil lamp.

decisions.choice: caña aplastada (L); mecha que apenas arde (L, B)
decisions.reason: Matthew 12:20 has "caña aplastada" and "mecha que apenas arde"; the same key words keep the quotation visible.

source.text: לֹ֤א יִכְהֶה֙ וְלֹ֣א יָר֔וּץ עַד־יָשִׂ֥ים בָּאָ֖רֶץ מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וּלְתוֹרָת֖וֹ אִיִּ֥ים יְיַחֵֽילוּ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Not he will grow dim, and not he will be crushed, until he sets on the earth justice; and for his instruction coastlands will wait.

en.L: He will not grow dim, and he will not be crushed, \q until he sets justice on the earth; \q and for his instruction the coastlands will wait.
en.B: He will not burn low or be crushed \q until he has set justice in place on the earth, \q and the coastlands will wait in hope for his instruction.
en.R: He will not fade or be broken \q until he makes justice firm on the earth. \q Lands far away will wait with hope for his teaching.

es.L: No se apagará ni se quebrará \q hasta que establezca la justicia en la tierra; \q y las costas esperarán su instrucción.
es.B: No se apagará ni se quebrará \q hasta que haya establecido la justicia en la tierra, \q y las costas lejanas esperarán con esperanza su instrucción.
es.R: No se debilitará ni se dará por vencido \q hasta que haga firme la justicia en la tierra. \q Las tierras lejanas esperarán con esperanza su enseñanza.

sw.L: Hatafifia, wala hatapondeka, \q mpaka atakapoweka haki duniani; \q na visiwa vitayangojea mafundisho yake.
sw.B: Hatazimika wala hatavunjika moyo \q mpaka atakapoisimika haki duniani, \q na pwani za mbali zitayangojea mafundisho yake kwa tumaini.
sw.R: Hatadhoofika wala hatavunjika \q mpaka atakapoifanya haki kuwa imara duniani. \q Nchi za mbali ng'ambo ya bahari zitasubiri mafundisho yake kwa matumaini.

decisions.choice: he will not grow dim or be crushed: a play on the words of verse 3
alternatives: he will not falter or be discouraged
decisions.reason: "Grow dim" is the word used of the wick, and "be crushed" the word used of the reed. The servant who spares the weak will not himself be put out or broken before his work is done.

decisions.choice: for his instruction the coastlands will wait
alternatives: in his name the nations will hope
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "his instruction". The Septuagint has "in his name nations will hope" (from memory; to be checked), and Matthew 12:21 quotes that form.

decisions.choice: coastlands: distant lands, the far edges of the known world
decisions.reason: The word means coasts and islands of the Mediterranean, and so the farthest lands (41:1, 5).

decisions.choice: se apagará; se quebrará
decisions.reason: The verbs repeat those of verse 3 ("la mecha que apenas arde", "la caña aplastada"); Spanish keeps the play with "apagarse" and "quebrarse".

decisions.choice: hatafifia ... hatapondeka (Literal); hatazimika ... hatavunjika (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The verbs echo the dim wick and the crushed reed of verse 3 (meaning decision m1); Literal keeps the same verbs, the other levels the nearest natural pair. God's torah is "mafundisho" here at every level, his teaching to the nations.

source.text: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֞ר הָאֵ֣ל׀יְהוָ֗ה בּוֹרֵ֤א הַשָּׁמַ֨יִם֙ וְנ֣וֹטֵיהֶ֔ם רֹקַ֥ע הָאָ֖רֶץ וְצֶאֱצָאֶ֑יהָ נֹתֵ֤ן נְשָׁמָה֙ לָעָ֣ם עָלֶ֔יהָ וְר֖וּחַ לַהֹלְכִ֥ים בָּֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says the God, the LORD, creating the heavens and stretching them out, beating out the earth and its produce, giving breath to the people on it and spirit to those walking in it:

en.L: Thus says the God, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, creator of the heavens and the one stretching them out, \q the one hammering out the earth and its offspring, \q giving breath to the people on it \q and spirit to those walking in it:
en.B: God, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, says this, the one who created the heavens and stretched them out, \q who hammered the earth flat and brought forth its growth, \q who gives breath to the people living on it \q and life to those who walk there:
en.R: This is what God, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, says. He created the sky and stretched it out. \q He spread out the earth and everything that grows on it. \q He gives breath to the people on the earth and life to all who walk on it.

es.L: Así dice el Dios, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, creador de los cielos y el que los extiende, \q el que expande la tierra y lo que de ella brota, \q el que da aliento al pueblo que hay sobre ella \q y espíritu a los que andan por ella:
es.B: Dios, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, dice esto, el que creó los cielos y los desplegó, \q el que extendió la tierra y lo que en ella crece, \q el que da aliento a la gente que vive en ella \q y vida a los que caminan por ella:
es.R: Esto es lo que dice Dios, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Él creó el cielo y lo extendió. \q Él extendió la tierra y todo lo que crece en ella. \q Él da aliento a la gente de la tierra y vida a todos los que andan por ella.

sw.L: Mungu, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, asema hivi, aliyeziumba mbingu na kuzitandaza, \q aliyeitandaza dunia na vitokavyo ndani yake, \q ampaye pumzi watu walio juu yake \q na roho wale waendao ndani yake:
sw.B: Hivi ndivyo Mungu, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, asemavyo, yeye aliyeziumba mbingu na kuzikunjua, \q aliyeitandaza nchi kama bamba na kuitoa mimea yake, \q awapaye pumzi watu wanaoishi juu yake \q na uhai wale wanaotembea humo:
sw.R: Hili ndilo Mungu, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, analosema. Yeye ndiye aliyeumba anga na kulitandaza. \q Alitandaza nchi na kila kitu kinachoota ndani yake. \q Huwapa pumzi watu walio duniani, na uhai wote wanaotembea juu yake.

decisions.choice: the creator speaks: the one who made and sustains the world commissions the servant
decisions.reason: The titles of God as maker of heaven and earth and giver of breath (40:22; Genesis 2:7) show that the one who calls the servant rules all peoples, which fits the servant's mission to the nations.

decisions.choice: beat out the earth and its produce: spread out the land and what grows from it
decisions.reason: The verb is used for hammering metal into a thin sheet. The noun means what comes out of the earth, its plants and offspring (34:1; 48:19).

decisions.choice: spirit: the breath of life
decisions.reason: Paired with "breath", the word means the life God gives to every living person, not the Spirit of verse 1.

decisions.choice: says this
decisions.reason: Balanced follows the settled wording for this formula; the colon introduces God's speech in verse 6.

decisions.choice: Así dice (L); dice esto (B); Esto es lo que dice (R)
decisions.reason: Book-wide for *koh amar* in this block, as the terms note sets it: L "Así dice el SEÑOR:", B "El SEÑOR dice esto:", R "Esto es lo que dice el SEÑOR:".

decisions.choice: Mungu, YHWH, asema hivi (Literal); Hivi ndivyo ... asemavyo (Balanced); Hili ndilo ... analosema (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Thus says the LORD" in the wording of 2 Kings 19:6, with God's titles following it as in the Hebrew. "Roho" (spirit) here is the breath of life (meaning decision m3), not the Spirit of verse 1, so Balanced and Readable say "uhai".

source.text: אֲנִ֧י יְהוָ֛ה קְרָאתִ֥יךָֽ בְצֶ֖דֶק וְאַחְזֵ֣ק בְּיָדֶ֑ךָ וְאֶצָּרְךָ֗ וְאֶתֶּנְךָ֛ לִבְרִ֥ית עָ֖ם לְא֥וֹר גּוֹיִֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: I, the LORD, I have called you in righteousness, and I will take hold of your hand and I will keep you, and I will give you for a covenant of [the] people, for a light of [the] nations,

en.L: I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have called you in righteousness, and I will take hold of your hand \q and I will keep you, and I will give you as a covenant of [the] people, as a light of [the] nations,
en.B: I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, called you for a righteous purpose; I will grip your hand and guard you. \q I will make you a covenant for the people and a light for the nations,
en.R: I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I have called you for a purpose that is right. I will hold your hand and keep you safe. \q I will make you a covenant for the people and a light for the nations.

es.L: Yo, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, te he llamado en justicia, y te tomaré de la mano \q y te guardaré, y te daré como pacto del pueblo, como luz de las naciones,
es.B: Yo, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, te llamé con un propósito justo; te tomaré firmemente de la mano y te protegeré. \q Te haré pacto para el pueblo y luz para las naciones,
es.R: Yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Te he llamado para un propósito que es justo. Te tomaré de la mano y te protegeré. \q Te haré un pacto para el pueblo y una luz para las naciones.

sw.L: Mimi, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nimekuita katika haki, nami nitakushika mkono wako \q na kukulinda, nami nitakutoa uwe agano la watu, nuru ya mataifa,
sw.B: Mimi, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nimekuita kwa kusudi la haki; nitakushika mkono na kukulinda. \q Nitakufanya uwe agano kwa ajili ya watu na nuru kwa mataifa,
sw.R: Mimi ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Nimekuita kwa kusudi lililo haki. Nitakushika mkono na kukulinda. \q Nitakufanya uwe agano kwa ajili ya watu na nuru kwa mataifa.

decisions.choice: in righteousness: in line with God's right and faithful purpose
decisions.reason: God's righteousness in these chapters is his faithful action to put things right and keep his promises (41:2, 10; 45:13). The servant is called as part of that purpose.

decisions.choice: a covenant for the people: the servant himself embodies God's covenant
decisions.reason: "The people" may be Israel, as in 49:8, where the same phrase is used of the servant restoring the land. Or it may be humankind, since verse 5 uses the same word for the people on the earth. Either way, the servant is the means by which God binds people to himself.

decisions.choice: a light for the nations
decisions.reason: The phrase returns in 49:6. Simeon echoes it of the child Jesus (Luke 2:32), and Paul and Barnabas apply 49:6 to their mission to the Gentiles (Acts 13:47).

decisions.choice: you: the servant of verse 1
decisions.reason: God now speaks to the servant directly. The sentence runs on into verse 7, which gives the purpose of the call.

decisions.choice: nuru ya mataifa (Literal); nuru kwa mataifa (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: "Nuru", light as a figure, the word of Luke 2:32 and Acts 13:47, which take up this phrase.

source.text: לִפְקֹ֖חַ עֵינַ֣יִם עִוְר֑וֹת לְהוֹצִ֤יא מִמַּסְגֵּר֙ אַסִּ֔יר מִבֵּ֥ית כֶּ֖לֶא יֹ֥שְׁבֵי חֹֽשֶׁךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: to open eyes blind, to bring out from [the] dungeon [the] prisoner, from [the] house of confinement [those] dwelling [in] darkness.

en.L: to open blind eyes, \q to bring out the prisoner from the dungeon, \q from the house of confinement those sitting in darkness.
en.B: to give sight to blind eyes, \q to lead captives out of their cells, \q and out of the prison house those who sit in darkness.
en.R: You will make blind eyes able to see. \q You will lead prisoners out of their cells. \q You will free those who sit in dark prisons.

es.L: para abrir los ojos ciegos, \q para sacar del calabozo al preso, \q de la casa de la cárcel a los que habitan en tinieblas.
es.B: para dar vista a los ojos ciegos, \q para sacar a los cautivos de sus celdas \q y de la prisión a los que están sentados en tinieblas.
es.R: Harás que los ojos ciegos puedan ver. \q Sacarás a los presos de sus celdas. \q Liberarás a los que están sentados en cárceles oscuras.

sw.L: kufumbua macho yaliyo vipofu, \q kumtoa mfungwa gerezani, \q kutoka nyumba ya kifungo wale wakaao gizani.
sw.B: kuyapa macho ya vipofu kuona, \q kuwatoa wafungwa katika vyumba vyao, \q na kutoka gerezani wale wanaoketi gizani.
sw.R: Utayafanya macho ya vipofu yaone. \q Utawaongoza wafungwa watoke katika vyumba vyao. \q Utawaweka huru wale wanaokaa katika magereza yenye giza.

decisions.choice: blind eyes, prisoners in darkness: release from exile and from spiritual blindness
decisions.reason: Blindness and prison describe Israel's state in exile (42:18-22), and also the nations who do not know God. Isaiah 61:1 joins sight and release in the same way, and Jesus reads that passage in Luke 4:18.

decisions.choice: You will
decisions.reason: Readable begins new sentences and supplies the subject, the servant addressed in verse 6.

source.text: אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה ה֣וּא שְׁמִ֑י וּכְבוֹדִי֙ לְאַחֵ֣ר לֹֽא־אֶתֵּ֔ן וּתְהִלָּתִ֖י לַפְּסִילִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: I [am] the LORD, that [is] my name; and my glory to another not I will give, and my praise to idols.

en.L: I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; that [is] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name; \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} glory to another I will not give, \q nor {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} praise to carved images.
en.B: I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; that is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name. \q My glory I will not hand over to anyone else, \q nor the praise due to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to carved images.
en.R: I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. That is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name. \q I will not let anyone else have {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} glory. \q I will not let idols take the praise that belongs to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: Yo [soy] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}; ese [es] {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre; \q y {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} gloria a otro no daré, \q ni {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} alabanza a las imágenes talladas.
es.B: Yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}; ese es {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre. \q No entregaré {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} gloria a ningún otro, \q ni la alabanza que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} corresponde a las imágenes talladas.
es.R: Yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Ese es {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre. \q No dejaré que nadie más se quede con {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} gloria. \q No dejaré que los ídolos reciban la alabanza que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} pertenece.

sw.L: Mimi [ni] {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}; hilo [ndilo] jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}; \q na utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} sitampa mwingine, \q wala sifa {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}} sanamu za kuchonga.
sw.B: Mimi ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}; hilo ndilo jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}. \q Utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} sitamkabidhi mwingine yeyote, \q wala sifa zinazonistahili sitazipa sanamu za kuchonga.
sw.R: Mimi ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Hilo ndilo jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}. \q Sitamwachia mtu mwingine utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}. \q Sitaziacha sanamu zichukue sifa zinazonistahili {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}.

decisions.choice: I am the LORD, that is my name: God's own name marks him as the only God
decisions.reason: God names himself by the name revealed to Moses (Exodus 3:15). In these chapters he repeatedly sets himself against the idols of the nations (40:18-20; 41:21-24; 44:6-20).

decisions.choice: carved images: idols shaped from wood or stone
decisions.reason: The word comes from a verb meaning to cut or carve (40:19-20).

source.text: הָרִֽאשֹׁנ֖וֹת הִנֵּה־בָ֑אוּ וַֽחֲדָשׁוֹת֙ אֲנִ֣י מַגִּ֔יד בְּטֶ֥רֶם תִּצְמַ֖חְנָה אַשְׁמִ֥יעאֶתְכֶֽם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: The former [things], see, they have come, and new [things] I [am] declaring; before they spring up I make you hear [them].

en.L: The former things, see, they have come, \q and new things I am declaring; \q before they sprout, I make you hear [of them].
en.B: Look, what was foretold long ago has come about, \q and now I announce things that are new. \q Before they begin to sprout, I let you hear of them.
en.R: Look, the things I told you about long ago have happened. \q Now I am telling you about new things. \q You hear about them from me before they start to happen.

es.L: Las cosas primeras, {{plural_you:miren|mirad}}, han sucedido, \q y cosas nuevas yo anuncio; \q antes que broten, {{plural_you:se las hago|os las hago}} oír.
es.B: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, lo que se anunció hace tiempo ya ha sucedido, \q y ahora anuncio cosas nuevas. \q Antes de que empiecen a brotar, {{plural_you:les|os}} hago saber de ellas.
es.R: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, las cosas que {{plural_you:les|os}} dije hace mucho tiempo han sucedido. \q Ahora {{plural_you:les|os}} hablo de cosas nuevas. \q {{plural_you:Ustedes oyen|Vosotros oís}} de ellas por mí antes de que empiecen a suceder.

sw.L: Mambo ya kwanza, tazama, yametokea, \q na mambo mapya ninayatangaza; \q kabla hayajachipuka, ninawasikizisha [habari zake].
sw.B: Tazama, yale yaliyotabiriwa zamani yametimia, \q na sasa ninatangaza mambo mapya. \q Kabla hayajaanza kuchipuka, ninawajulisha.
sw.R: Tazama, mambo niliyowaambia zamani yametokea. \q Sasa ninawaambia mambo mapya. \q Mnayasikia kutoka kwangu kabla hayajaanza kutokea.

decisions.choice: the former things: earlier events that God announced and brought about
decisions.reason: In these chapters God proves he is God by announcing events before they happen (41:22-23; 43:9; 48:3-6). The "new things" are the coming release from exile and what follows.

decisions.choice: before they sprout: before there is any sign of them
decisions.reason: The new events are pictured as plants that have not yet come up out of the ground (43:19).

decisions.choice: what was foretold; the things I told you about
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that the former things are events God had announced, which the argument of verse 9 assumes.

source.text: שִׁ֤ירוּ לַֽיהוָה֙ שִׁ֣יר חָדָ֔שׁ תְּהִלָּת֖וֹ מִקְצֵ֣ה הָאָ֑רֶץ יוֹרְדֵ֤י הַיָּם֙ וּמְלֹא֔וֹ אִיִּ֖ים וְיֹשְׁבֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Sing to the LORD a song new, his praise from [the] end of the earth, [you] going down [to] the sea and its fullness, coastlands and their inhabitants.

en.L: Sing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} a new song, \q {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} praise from the end of the earth, \q [you] who go down to the sea, and all that fills it, \q coastlands and their inhabitants.
en.B: Sing {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} a new song; \q let {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} praise sound from the far edge of the earth, \q you seafarers and everything that fills the sea, \q you coastlands and all who dwell on them.
en.R: Sing a new song to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! \q Praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from the farthest places on earth. \q Praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, you sailors and everything that lives in the sea. \q Praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, you lands far away and all who live there.

es.L: {{plural_you:Canten|Cantad}} {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} un cántico nuevo, \q {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} alabanza desde el extremo de la tierra, \q los que descienden al mar y lo que lo llena, \q las costas y sus habitantes.
es.B: {{plural_you:Canten|Cantad}} {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} un cántico nuevo; \q que {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} alabanza resuene desde el confín de la tierra, \q {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, navegantes, y todo lo que llena el mar, \q costas lejanas y todos los que habitan en ellas.
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Canten|Cantad}} una canción nueva {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}! \q {{plural_you:Alábenlo|Alabadlo}} desde los lugares más lejanos de la tierra. \q {{plural_you:Alábenlo|Alabadlo}}, marineros, y todo lo que vive en el mar. \q {{plural_you:Alábenlo|Alabadlo}}, tierras lejanas, y todos los que viven allí.

sw.L: Mwimbieni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wimbo mpya, \q sifa {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} tangu mwisho wa dunia, \q [ninyi] mshukao baharini, na vyote vilivyomo, \q visiwa na wakaao humo.
sw.B: Mwimbieni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wimbo mpya; \q sifa {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} na zisikike kutoka mwisho wa dunia, \q enyi wasafiri wa baharini na vyote vilivyomo baharini, \q enyi pwani za mbali na wote wakaao huko.
sw.R: Mwimbieni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wimbo mpya! \q Msifuni kutoka sehemu za mbali kabisa duniani. \q Msifuni, enyi mabaharia na kila kiumbe kinachoishi baharini. \q Msifuni, enyi nchi za mbali ng'ambo ya bahari na wote wanaoishi huko.

decisions.choice: a new song: praise for a new act of God
decisions.reason: The call echoes the psalms (Psalm 96:1; 98:1). The song is new because it answers the "new things" of verse 9.

decisions.choice: those who go down to the sea: sailors and seafaring traders
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used of merchants who sail in ships (Psalm 107:23). The call reaches from the sea to the desert (verse 11), so the whole world is included. Psalm 96:11 and 98:7 have the similar line "let the sea roar, and all that fills it".

decisions.choice: Praise him ... Praise him
decisions.reason: Readable repeats the call to praise for each group in short sentences.

source.text: יִשְׂא֤וּ מִדְבָּר֙ וְעָרָ֔יו חֲצֵרִ֖ים תֵּשֵׁ֣ב קֵדָ֑ר יָרֹ֨נּוּ֙ יֹ֣שְׁבֵי סֶ֔לַע מֵרֹ֥אשׁ הָרִ֖ים יִצְוָֽחוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Let them lift up [the] wilderness and its cities, [the] villages [where] Kedar dwells; let them shout for joy, [the] inhabitants of Sela; from [the] top of [the] mountains let them cry aloud.

en.L: Let the wilderness and its cities lift up [their voice], \q the villages where Kedar dwells; \q let the inhabitants of Sela shout for joy; \q from the top of the mountains let them cry aloud.
en.B: Let the desert and its towns lift their voices, \q the camps where Kedar's people live; \q let those who live in Sela ring out with joy, \q calling out from the peaks of the mountains.
en.R: Let the desert and its towns shout. \q Let the camps where the tribes of Kedar live join in. \q Let the people of Sela sing with joy. \q Let them shout from the tops of the mountains.

es.L: Que alcen [la voz] el desierto y sus ciudades, \q las aldeas donde habita Cedar; \q que canten de júbilo los habitantes de Sela; \q desde la cumbre de los montes que griten.
es.B: Que el desierto y sus pueblos alcen la voz, \q los campamentos donde vive la gente de Cedar; \q que los que habitan en Sela canten con júbilo, \q gritando desde las cimas de los montes.
es.R: Que el desierto y sus pueblos griten. \q Que se unan los campamentos donde viven las tribus de Cedar. \q Que la gente de Sela cante con alegría. \q Que griten desde las cimas de los montes.

sw.L: Nyika na miji yake na viinue [sauti zao], \q vijiji akaamo Kedari; \q wakaao Sela na waimbe kwa furaha; \q kutoka vilele vya milima na wapige kelele.
sw.B: Jangwa na miji yake na vipaze sauti, \q makambi wanamoishi watu wa Kedari; \q wakaao Sela na waimbe kwa shangwe, \q wakipiga kelele kutoka vilele vya milima.
sw.R: Jangwa na miji yake na vipige kelele. \q Makambi wanamoishi makabila ya Kedari na yajiunge nao. \q Watu wa Sela na waimbe kwa furaha. \q Na wapige kelele kutoka vilele vya milima.

decisions.choice: Kedar: Arab tribes of the desert east of Israel
decisions.reason: Kedar was a son of Ishmael (Genesis 25:13). His descendants were herders who lived in tent camps and unwalled villages (21:16-17; 60:7).

decisions.choice: Sela: a place in the rocky land of Edom, or the rocky heights generally
alternatives: those who live among the rocks
decisions.reason: The name means "rock". A town called Sela in Edom is named in 2 Kings 14:7 and Isaiah 16:1. Here it may be that town, or simply people who live among the crags.

decisions.choice: lift up [their voice]
decisions.reason: The verb has no object; the sense is raising the voice in song.

source.text: יָשִׂ֥ימוּ לַֽיהוָ֖ה כָּב֑וֹד וּתְהִלָּת֖וֹ בָּאִיִּ֥ים יַגִּֽידוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Let them give to the LORD glory, and his praise in the coastlands let them declare.

en.L: Let them give to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} glory, \q and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} praise in the coastlands let them declare.
en.B: Let them bring glory to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} \q and spread {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} praise through the coastlands.
en.R: Let them give glory to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q Let them praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in lands far away.

es.L: Que den {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} gloria, \q y {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} alabanza en las costas anuncien.
es.B: Que den gloria {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} \q y difundan {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} alabanza por las costas lejanas.
es.R: Que den gloria {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. \q Que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} alaben en las tierras lejanas.

sw.L: Na wampe {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} utukufu, \q na sifa {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} katika visiwa na wazitangaze.
sw.B: Na wamletee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} utukufu \q na kueneza sifa {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} katika pwani za mbali.
sw.R: Na wampe {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} utukufu. \q Na wamsifu katika nchi za mbali ng'ambo ya bahari.

decisions.choice: let them: the desert peoples of verse 11 and all the world
decisions.reason: The call to praise that began at the ends of the earth (verse 10) ends with the coastlands, the far-off lands that wait for the servant's instruction (verse 4).

source.text: יְהוָה֙ כַּגִּבּ֣וֹר יֵצֵ֔א כְּאִ֥ישׁ מִלְחָמ֖וֹת יָעִ֣יר קִנְאָ֑ה יָרִ֨יעַ֙ אַף־יַצְרִ֔יחַ עַל־אֹיְבָ֖יו יִתְגַּבָּֽר׃ס

records.literal_gloss: The LORD like a warrior will go out, like a man of wars he will stir up zeal; he will shout, also he will raise a battle cry; over his enemies he will show himself mighty.

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} like a warrior will go out; \q like a man of war {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will stir up zeal; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will shout, yes, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will raise a battle cry; \q against {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} enemies {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will show {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} mighty.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will go out like a hero; \q like a seasoned soldier {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will fire up {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} zeal. \q He will shout, yes, raise the battle roar, \q and prove {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} strength against {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} enemies.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will go out like a strong soldier. \q Like a fighter ready for war, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is eager for battle. \q He will shout a loud war cry. \q He will show {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power over {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} enemies.

es.L: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} como guerrero saldrá; \q como hombre de guerra {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} despertará [su] celo; \q gritará, sí, lanzará el grito de guerra; \q contra {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} enemigos se mostrará poderoso.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} saldrá como un héroe; \q como un soldado curtido encenderá {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} celo. \q Gritará, sí, lanzará el rugido de batalla, \q y mostrará {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} fuerza contra {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} enemigos.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} saldrá como un soldado fuerte. \q Como un luchador listo para la guerra, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} tiene ganas de combatir. \q Lanzará un fuerte grito de guerra. \q Mostrará {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} poder sobre {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} enemigos.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atatoka kama shujaa; \q kama mtu wa vita ataamsha wivu; \q atapiga kelele, naam, atapiga kelele ya vita; \q juu ya adui {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} atajionyesha mwenye nguvu.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atatoka kama shujaa; \q kama askari aliyezoea vita atachochea wivu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. \q Atapiga kelele, naam, atanguruma kwa kelele ya vita, \q na kuonyesha nguvu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} juu ya adui {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atatoka kama askari hodari. \q Kama mpiganaji aliye tayari kwa vita, ana hamu ya kupigana. \q Atapiga ukelele mkubwa wa vita. \q Ataonyesha nguvu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} juu ya adui {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}.

decisions.choice: the LORD as a warrior: God going out to fight for his people
decisions.reason: Scripture pictures God as a warrior who fights for Israel (Exodus 15:3; Psalm 24:8). The servant is gentle (verses 2-3), but the God who sends him acts with power against his enemies, here the powers that hold his people captive.

decisions.choice: zeal: burning devotion that moves to action
decisions.reason: The word is used of jealous love that will not share what belongs to it (9:6; 37:32). Here it is God's passion for his people and his name (verse 8).

decisions.choice: eager for battle
decisions.reason: Readable says what stirring up zeal means for a fighter going to war.

source.text: הֶחֱשֵׁ֨יתִי֙ מֵֽעוֹלָ֔ם אַחֲרִ֖ישׁ אֶתְאַפָּ֑ק כַּיּוֹלֵדָ֣ה אֶפְעֶ֔ה אֶשֹּׁ֥ם וְאֶשְׁאַ֖ף יָֽחַד׃

records.literal_gloss: I have been silent from long ago; I have kept quiet; I have restrained myself; like the [woman] giving birth I will groan; I will gasp and I will pant together.

en.L: I have been silent from long ago; \q I have kept still; I have restrained {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}; \q like a woman giving birth I will groan; \q I will gasp and pant at once.
en.B: Long have I been silent; \q I have kept still and held {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} in check. \q Now I will groan like a woman giving birth, \q gasping and panting at once.
en.R: For a long time I have said nothing. \q I have stayed quiet and kept {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} from acting. \q But now I will cry out like a woman having a baby. \q I will gasp and breathe hard.

es.L: He callado desde hace mucho; \q he guardado silencio; me he contenido; \q como la que da a luz gemiré; \q jadearé y resoplaré a la vez.
es.B: Por mucho tiempo he callado; \q he guardado silencio y me he contenido. \q Ahora gemiré como mujer que da a luz, \q jadeando y resoplando a la vez.
es.R: Durante mucho tiempo no he dicho nada. \q Me he quedado callado y no he actuado. \q Pero ahora gritaré como una mujer que está dando a luz. \q Jadearé y respiraré con fuerza.

sw.L: Nimenyamaza tangu zamani; \q nimetulia; nimejizuia; \q kama mwanamke azaaye nitaugua; \q nitatweta na kuhema pamoja.
sw.B: Kwa muda mrefu nimenyamaza; \q nimetulia na kujizuia. \q Sasa nitaugua kama mwanamke anayejifungua, \q nikitweta na kuhema kwa pamoja.
sw.R: Kwa muda mrefu sikusema kitu. \q Nimekaa kimya na kujizuia nisitende. \q Lakini sasa nitalia kama mwanamke anayejifungua mtoto. \q Nitatweta na kupumua kwa nguvu.

decisions.choice: I have been silent ... I will groan: a long waiting ends in sudden action
decisions.reason: The first three verbs describe the long time God held back while his people were in exile. The next verbs describe what he is about to do. The change of verb forms marks the turn from waiting to acting.

decisions.choice: like a woman giving birth: intense effort that brings something new
decisions.reason: The picture of labor pains usually describes terror (13:8; 21:3). Here God himself is the one in labor: the strain of the moment when he brings his new things to birth (verse 9).

decisions.choice: Now; But now
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable mark the change from waiting to acting that the Hebrew shows by the change of verb forms.

source.text: אַחֲרִ֤יב הָרִים֙ וּגְבָע֔וֹת וְכָל־עֶשְׂבָּ֖ם אוֹבִ֑ישׁ וְשַׂמְתִּ֤י נְהָרוֹת֙ לָֽאִיִּ֔ים וַאֲגַמִּ֖ים אוֹבִֽישׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: I will lay waste mountains and hills, and all their vegetation I will dry up; and I will make rivers into islands, and pools I will dry up.

en.L: I will lay waste mountains and hills, \q and all their vegetation I will dry up; \q and I will make rivers into islands, \q and pools I will dry up.
en.B: I will strip mountains and hills bare \q and parch every green thing on them. \q I will turn rivers into dry land \q and leave the marsh pools dry.
en.R: I will destroy the mountains and hills and dry up all the plants on them. \q I will turn rivers into dry land. \q I will dry up the ponds.

es.L: Asolaré montes y collados, \q y toda su hierba secaré; \q y convertiré los ríos en islas, \q y los estanques secaré.
es.B: Dejaré pelados los montes y las colinas \q y secaré todo su verdor. \q Convertiré los ríos en tierra seca \q y dejaré secos los pantanos.
es.R: Destruiré los montes y las colinas y secaré todas sus plantas. \q Convertiré los ríos en tierra seca. \q Secaré las lagunas.

sw.L: Nitaifanya milima na vilima kuwa ukiwa, \q na mimea yake yote nitaikausha; \q nami nitaifanya mito kuwa visiwa, \q na madimbwi nitayakausha.
sw.B: Nitaiacha milima na vilima wazi \q na kukausha kila kitu kibichi juu yake. \q Nitaigeuza mito kuwa nchi kavu \q na kuyaacha madimbwi yakiwa makavu.
sw.R: Nitaiharibu milima na vilima na kukausha mimea yote iliyo juu yake. \q Nitaigeuza mito kuwa nchi kavu. \q Nitakausha mabwawa.

decisions.choice: islands: here, dry ground standing out of the water
decisions.reason: The word usually means coastlands or islands. Here rivers are dried up until only land remains, so it means dry ground.

decisions.choice: God's power over the land: turning the world upside down for his purpose
decisions.reason: Elsewhere God turns desert into pools (41:18; 43:19-20). Here he does the reverse against his enemies, showing the same power over nature that he used at the Red Sea (50:2; Exodus 14:21).

decisions.choice: dry land
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the word here; Literal keeps "islands".

source.text: וְהוֹלַכְתִּ֣י עִוְרִ֗ים בְּדֶ֨רֶךְ֙ לֹ֣א יָדָ֔עוּ בִּנְתִיב֥וֹת לֹֽא־יָדְע֖וּ אַדְרִיכֵ֑ם אָשִׂים֩ מַחְשָׁ֨ךְ לִפְנֵיהֶ֜ם לָא֗וֹר וּמַֽעֲקַשִּׁים֙ לְמִישׁ֔וֹר אֵ֚לֶּה הַדְּבָרִ֔ים עֲשִׂיתִ֖ם וְלֹ֥א עֲזַבְתִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will lead blind [people] by a way [which] not they have known; in paths [which] not they have known I will make them walk; I will make [the] darkness before them into light, and rough places into level ground. These [are] the things [which] I will do them, and not I will abandon them.

en.L: And I will lead the blind by a way they have not known; \q in paths they have not known I will make them walk; \q I will turn the darkness before them into light, and rough places into level ground. \q These [are] the things I will do, and I will not abandon them.
en.B: I will lead the blind on a road strange to them \q and guide them along tracks they have never walked. \q Ahead of them I will change darkness to light and rough ground to level. \q This is what I will do; I will not abandon them.
en.R: I will lead people who are blind on a road they do not know. \q I will guide them along paths they have never seen. \q I will turn the darkness in front of them into light. \q I will make the rough ground smooth. \q I will do these things. I will not leave {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people alone.

es.L: Y conduciré a los ciegos por un camino que no conocieron; \q por senderos que no conocieron los haré andar; \q convertiré delante de ellos las tinieblas en luz, y los lugares escabrosos en llanura. \q Estas [son] las cosas que haré, y no los abandonaré.
es.B: Llevaré a los ciegos por un camino que no conocen \q y los guiaré por sendas que nunca han pisado. \q Delante de ellos cambiaré las tinieblas en luz y el terreno áspero en llano. \q Esto es lo que haré; no los abandonaré.
es.R: Llevaré a los que están ciegos por un camino que no conocen. \q Los guiaré por senderos que nunca han visto. \q Convertiré en luz la oscuridad que tienen delante. \q Haré llano el terreno áspero. \q Haré estas cosas. No dejaré solo a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo.

sw.L: Nami nitawaongoza vipofu kwa njia wasiyoijua; \q katika mapito wasiyoyajua nitawaendesha; \q nitaigeuza giza mbele yao kuwa nuru, na mahali palipoparuza kuwa tambarare. \q Haya [ndiyo] mambo nitakayoyafanya, wala sitawaacha.
sw.B: Nitawaongoza vipofu katika njia wasiyoifahamu \q na kuwaelekeza katika mapito ambayo hawajawahi kuyapita. \q Mbele yao nitageuza giza kuwa nuru na ardhi iliyoparuza kuwa sawa. \q Hili ndilo nitakalofanya; sitawaacha.
sw.R: Nitawaongoza watu walio vipofu katika njia wasiyoijua. \q Nitawaelekeza katika mapito ambayo hawajawahi kuyaona. \q Nitaligeuza giza lililo mbele yao kuwa nuru. \q Nitafanya ardhi iliyoparuza iwe laini. \q Nitafanya mambo haya. Sitawaacha watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} peke yao.

decisions.choice: the blind: God's people, who cannot find the way home by themselves
decisions.reason: The blind here are those God brings home from exile. Verses 18-19 show that Israel itself is blind.

decisions.choice: I will not abandon them: God will not leave the blind he is leading
alternatives: I will not leave these things undone
decisions.reason: "Them" most naturally refers to the blind people of the verse. It could instead mean the things God has promised: he will not leave them undone. The verb for "I will do" is a past form used for what is certain.

decisions.choice: my people
decisions.reason: Readable names the blind of this verse as God's people, following the meaning decision.

source.text: נָסֹ֤גוּ אָחוֹר֙ יֵבֹ֣שׁוּ בֹ֔שֶׁת הַבֹּטְחִ֖ים בַּפָּ֑סֶל הָאֹמְרִ֥ים לְמַסֵּכָ֖ה אַתֶּ֥ם אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: They will be turned back; they will be ashamed [with] shame, those trusting in an idol, those saying to a molten image, You [are] our gods.

en.L: They will be turned back; they will be utterly put to shame, \q those who trust in a carved idol, \q who say to a cast image, "You [are] our gods."
en.B: But those who rely on a carved idol \q and say to a cast image, "You are our gods," \q will be forced to retreat, covered with shame.
en.R: But people who trust in idols will turn back in shame. \q They say to statues made of metal, "You are our gods."

es.L: Serán vueltos atrás, serán avergonzados con vergüenza \q los que confían en el ídolo tallado, \q los que dicen a la imagen fundida: «{{plural_you:Ustedes [son]|Vosotros [sois]}} nuestros dioses».
es.B: Pero los que confían en un ídolo tallado \q y dicen a una imagen fundida: «{{plural_you:Ustedes son|Vosotros sois}} nuestros dioses», \q tendrán que retroceder, cubiertos de vergüenza.
es.R: Pero los que confían en ídolos se darán la vuelta llenos de vergüenza. \q Les dicen a estatuas de metal: «{{plural_you:Ustedes son|Vosotros sois}} nuestros dioses».

sw.L: Watarudishwa nyuma; wataaibishwa kabisa, \q wale wanaotumainia sanamu ya kuchonga, \q wanaoiambia sanamu ya kuyeyushwa, "Ninyi [ni] miungu yetu."
sw.B: Lakini wale wanaoitegemea sanamu ya kuchonga \q na kuiambia sanamu ya kuyeyushwa, "Ninyi ni miungu yetu," \q watalazimishwa kurudi nyuma wakiwa wamejaa aibu.
sw.R: Lakini watu wanaotumainia sanamu watarudi nyuma kwa aibu. \q Wanaziambia sanamu zilizotengenezwa kwa chuma, "Ninyi ni miungu yetu."

decisions.choice: a carved idol, a cast image: idols of wood or stone and idols of poured metal
decisions.reason: The two words name the two ways idols were made: carved and then overlaid, or cast in molten metal (40:19; 44:10).

decisions.choice: turned back and put to shame: defeated and disgraced
decisions.reason: "Turned back" is the language of an army forced to retreat. The doubled "shame" makes the disgrace complete.

decisions.choice: But
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable mark the contrast between those God leads (verse 16) and those who trust in idols.

source.text: הַחֵרְשִׁ֖ים שְׁמָ֑עוּ וְהַעִוְרִ֖ים הַבִּ֥יטוּ לִרְאֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: O deaf [ones], listen! and O blind [ones], look to see!

en.L: You deaf ones, listen! \q And you blind ones, look, so as to see!
en.B: You deaf ones, listen! \q You blind ones, look up and see!
en.R: Listen, you people who are deaf! \q Look, you people who are blind, so that you can see!

es.L: ¡Sordos, {{plural_you:oigan|oíd}}! \q ¡Y ciegos, {{plural_you:miren|mirad}} para ver!
es.B: ¡Sordos, {{plural_you:escuchen|escuchad}}! \q ¡Ciegos, {{plural_you:levanten|levantad}} los ojos y {{plural_you:vean|ved}}!
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}, {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} que son sordos! \q ¡{{plural_you:Miren, ustedes que son ciegos, para que puedan|Mirad, vosotros que sois ciegos, para que podáis}} ver!

sw.L: Enyi viziwi, sikieni! \q Nanyi vipofu, tazameni, mpate kuona!
sw.B: Enyi viziwi, sikilizeni! \q Enyi vipofu, inueni macho mwone!
sw.R: Sikilizeni, enyi watu viziwi! \q Tazameni, enyi watu vipofu, ili mpate kuona!

decisions.choice: the deaf and the blind: Israel, who will not take in what God shows and says
decisions.reason: Verse 19 identifies the blind and deaf as God's servant, and verse 24 names Jacob and Israel. Their blindness recalls the hardening announced in 6:9-10.

source.text: מִ֤י עִוֵּר֙ כִּ֣י אִם־עַבְדִּ֔י וְחֵרֵ֖שׁ כְּמַלְאָכִ֣י אֶשְׁלָ֑ח מִ֤י עִוֵּר֙ כִּמְשֻׁלָּ֔ם וְעִוֵּ֖ר כְּעֶ֥בֶד יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Who [is] blind but my servant, and deaf like my messenger [whom] I send? Who [is] blind like [the] one in covenant, and blind like the servant of the LORD?

en.L: Who [is] blind but {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant, \q or deaf like {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} messenger [whom] I send? \q Who [is] blind like the dedicated one, \q and blind like the servant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}?
en.B: Who is so blind as {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant, \q so deaf as the messenger I am sending? \q Who is as blind as the dedicated one, \q as blind as the servant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}?
en.R: No one is as blind as {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant Israel. \q No one is as deaf as the messenger I am sending. \q No one is as blind as the one I have set apart, \q the servant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: ¿Quién [es] ciego sino {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo, \q o sordo como {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mensajero [a quien] envío? \q ¿Quién [es] ciego como el consagrado, \q y ciego como el siervo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}?
es.B: ¿Quién es tan ciego como {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo, \q tan sordo como el mensajero que envío? \q ¿Quién es tan ciego como el consagrado, \q tan ciego como el siervo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}?
es.R: Nadie es tan ciego como {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo Israel. \q Nadie es tan sordo como el mensajero que envío. \q Nadie es tan ciego como aquel que he apartado para mí, \q el siervo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Ni nani [aliye] kipofu ila mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, \q au kiziwi kama mjumbe {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} [ninayemtuma]? \q Ni nani [aliye] kipofu kama yule aliyejitoa, \q na kipofu kama mtumishi wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}?
sw.B: Ni nani aliye kipofu kama mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, \q kiziwi kama mjumbe ninayemtuma? \q Ni nani aliye kipofu kama yule aliyewekwa wakfu, \q kipofu kama mtumishi wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}?
sw.R: Hakuna aliye kipofu kama mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} Israeli. \q Hakuna aliye kiziwi kama mjumbe ninayemtuma. \q Hakuna aliye kipofu kama yule niliyemtenga kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, \q mtumishi wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

decisions.choice: my servant, blind and deaf: Israel, called to serve but failing to see
decisions.reason: The same title given to the faithful servant of verse 1 is here given to Israel, who is blind and deaf (verses 18, 24). The servant of verses 1-4 opens blind eyes (verse 7); this servant needs his own eyes opened. See the note at 41:8.

decisions.choice: the dedicated one: one given over to God, or at peace with him
alternatives: the one at peace with me
decisions.reason: The word comes from the root meaning whole or at peace. It may mean one in a covenant of peace with God, one dedicated to him, or one whom God has repaid. The sense is uncertain.

decisions.choice: No one is as blind as ...; my servant Israel
decisions.reason: Readable turns the questions, which expect the answer "no one", into statements, and names the servant as Israel from verse 24.

source.text: רָא֥וֹת רַבּ֖וֹת וְלֹ֣א תִשְׁמֹ֑ר פָּק֥וֹחַ אָזְנַ֖יִם וְלֹ֥א יִשְׁמָֽע׃

records.literal_gloss: Seeing many [things], and not you observe; opening [the] ears, and not he hears.

en.L: Seeing many things, but you do not keep [them]; \q opening [the] ears, but he does not hear.
en.B: You see so much, yet you take no notice; \q his ears are open, yet he hears nothing.
en.R: You see many things, but you ignore them. \q Your ears are open, but you hear nothing.

es.L: Viendo muchas cosas, pero no [las] guardas; \q abriendo los oídos, pero no oye.
es.B: Ves tantas cosas, y no prestas atención; \q tiene los oídos abiertos, y no oye nada.
es.R: Ves muchas cosas, pero no les haces caso. \q Tienes los oídos abiertos, pero no oyes nada.

sw.L: Ukiona mambo mengi, lakini huyashiki; \q masikio yakiwa wazi, lakini yeye hasikii.
sw.B: Unaona mambo mengi, lakini huyajali; \q masikio yake yako wazi, lakini hasikii kitu.
sw.R: Unaona mambo mengi, lakini huyajali. \q Masikio yako yako wazi, lakini husikii chochote.

decisions.choice: seeing: the reading of the margin (qere)
decisions.reason: The written text (ketiv) has "you have seen" and the margin has "seeing", an infinitive. The sense is the same: much has been seen, but nothing taken in.

decisions.choice: you ... he: the speaker turns from addressing Israel to speaking about him
decisions.reason: Such changes of person are common in Hebrew poetry. Both lines refer to the same blind and deaf servant.

decisions.choice: Your ears ... you hear nothing
decisions.reason: Readable keeps "you" in both lines so young readers do not lose track of who is meant; Literal and Balanced keep the change of person.

source.text: יְהוָ֥ה חָפֵ֖ץ לְמַ֣עַן צִדְק֑וֹ יַגְדִּ֥יל תּוֹרָ֖ה וְיַאְדִּֽיר׃

records.literal_gloss: The LORD was pleased for the sake of his righteousness; he will make great [the] instruction and he will make [it] glorious.

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was pleased, for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} righteousness, \q to make [the] instruction great and to make [it] glorious.
en.B: For the sake of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own righteousness, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was glad \q to make the instruction great and splendid.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} wanted to show that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does what is right. \q So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} teaching great and wonderful.

es.L: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se complació, por amor de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} justicia, \q en engrandecer la instrucción y hacer[la] gloriosa.
es.B: Por amor de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} propia justicia, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} quiso \q hacer grande y espléndida la instrucción.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} quería mostrar que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} hace lo que es justo. \q Por eso hizo que {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} enseñanza fuera grande y maravillosa.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alipendezwa, kwa ajili ya haki {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, \q kuyafanya mafundisho kuwa makuu na kuyafanya [kuwa] ya utukufu.
sw.B: Kwa ajili ya haki {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} mwenyewe, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alifurahi \q kuyakuza mafundisho na kuyafanya yawe ya fahari.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alitaka kuonyesha kwamba {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} hutenda yaliyo haki. \q Kwa hiyo aliyafanya mafundisho {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kuwa makuu na ya ajabu.

decisions.choice: his righteousness: God's faithfulness to his own just purpose
decisions.reason: God's righteousness is his faithfulness to what is right and to his promises (verse 6). Because of it he gave Israel his instruction, so that the failure described next is all the more serious.

decisions.choice: instruction: God's teaching given to Israel
decisions.reason: The word means teaching, especially the instruction God gave his people through Moses and the prophets (1:10; 2:3). It is the instruction the coastlands wait for in verse 4 and that Israel did not obey in verse 24.

decisions.choice: wanted to show that he does what is right; his teaching
decisions.reason: Readable explains "for the sake of his righteousness" and supplies whose teaching it is.

decisions.choice: instrucción (L, B); enseñanza (R)
decisions.reason: *Torah* is "instrucción" at Literal and Balanced and "enseñanza" at Readable, as in the Psalms; book-wide in this block.

decisions.choice: mafundisho
decisions.reason: God's torah here is his instruction given to Israel (meaning decision m2); the Psalms note's "sheria" at Literal is set aside in Isaiah, whose torah is teaching to be heard, and "mafundisho" stands at every level, as in 42:4.

source.text: וְהוּא֮ עַם־בָּז֣וּז וְשָׁסוּי֒ הָפֵ֤חַ בַּֽחוּרִים֙ כֻּלָּ֔ם וּבְבָתֵּ֥י כְלָאִ֖ים הָחְבָּ֑אוּ הָי֤וּ לָבַז֙ וְאֵ֣ין מַצִּ֔יל מְשִׁסָּ֖ה וְאֵין־אֹמֵ֥ר הָשַֽׁב׃

records.literal_gloss: But it [is] a people plundered and looted; trapped in holes all of them, and in houses of prison they are hidden; they have become plunder, and there is no deliverer; spoil, and there is no one saying, Give back!

en.L: But this [is] a people plundered and looted; \q all of them trapped in holes, \q and in houses of prison they are hidden; \q they have become plunder, and there is no one to rescue; \q spoil, and there is no one saying, "Bring [them] back!"
en.B: Yet they are a people robbed and stripped, \q every one of them snared in holes \q and locked away in jails. \q They have become prey with none to rescue, \q booty with none to say, "Return them!"
en.R: But these people have been robbed of everything. \q All of them are trapped in holes or hidden away in prisons. \q Enemies carried them off like loot, and no one saves them. \q No one says, "Give them back!"

es.L: Pero este [es] un pueblo saqueado y despojado; \q todos ellos atrapados en hoyos, \q y en casas de prisión están escondidos; \q han venido a ser botín, y no hay quien libre; \q despojo, y no hay quien diga: «¡Devuelve[los]!».
es.B: Pero es un pueblo robado y despojado, \q todos ellos atrapados en agujeros \q y encerrados en cárceles. \q Se han convertido en presa y nadie los rescata, \q en botín y nadie dice: «¡Devuélvelos!».
es.R: Pero a este pueblo le han robado todo. \q Todos están atrapados en agujeros o escondidos en cárceles. \q Los enemigos se los llevaron como botín, y nadie los salva. \q Nadie dice: «¡Devuélvelos!».

sw.L: Lakini hili [ni] taifa lililonyang'anywa na kutekwa; \q wote wamenaswa mashimoni, \q na katika nyumba za gereza wamefichwa; \q wamekuwa mateka, wala hakuna wa kuokoa; \q nyara, wala hakuna asemaye, "Warudisheni!"
sw.B: Hata hivyo ni watu walioporwa na kunyang'anywa kila kitu, \q kila mmoja wao amenaswa katika mashimo \q na kufungiwa magerezani. \q Wamekuwa mawindo bila mtu wa kuwaokoa, \q nyara bila mtu wa kusema, "Warudishe!"
sw.R: Lakini watu hawa wamenyang'anywa kila kitu. \q Wote wamenaswa mashimoni au kufichwa magerezani. \q Adui waliwachukua kama nyara, wala hakuna anayewaokoa. \q Hakuna anayesema, "Warudisheni!"

decisions.choice: trapped in holes: the reading of the standard vowels
alternatives: all their young men are trapped
decisions.reason: The consonants could also be read "all their young men" with different vowels. The standard reading fits the parallel line about prisons.

decisions.choice: plundered and looted: Israel defeated and carried off
decisions.reason: The words describe the spoils taken in war. Israel's exile is pictured as a people stripped bare and held in prison with no one to demand their return.

decisions.choice: Enemies carried them off
decisions.reason: Readable names who did the plundering, which the passive verbs leave unstated.

source.text: מִ֥י בָכֶ֖ם יַאֲזִ֣ין זֹ֑את יַקְשִׁ֥ב וְיִשְׁמַ֖ע לְאָחֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: Who among you will give ear [to] this, will pay attention and will listen for [the time] afterward?

en.L: Who among you will give ear to this, \q will pay attention and listen for the time to come?
en.B: Which one of you will open your ears to this, \q attend closely, and listen from now on?
en.R: Will any of you listen to this? \q Will you pay attention and listen from now on?

es.L: ¿Quién entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} prestará oído a esto, \q atenderá y escuchará en lo por venir?
es.B: ¿Quién de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} abrirá sus oídos a esto, \q pondrá atención y escuchará de ahora en adelante?
es.R: ¿Alguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} escuchará esto? \q ¿{{plural_you:Prestarán atención y escucharán|Prestaréis atención y escucharéis}} de ahora en adelante?

sw.L: Ni nani miongoni mwenu atakayetega sikio kwa hili, \q atakayesikiliza na kusikia kwa ajili ya wakati ujao?
sw.B: Ni yupi kati yenu atakayeyafungua masikio yake kwa jambo hili, \q akasikiliza kwa makini na kusikia tangu sasa?
sw.R: Je, kuna yeyote kati yenu atakayesikiliza jambo hili? \q Mtasikiliza kwa makini tangu sasa?

decisions.choice: for the time to come: from now on, so as to learn for the future
decisions.reason: The question looks for someone who will take the lesson of Israel's suffering to heart for the future, unlike those described in verses 20 and 25.

source.text: מִֽי־נָתַ֨ן לִמְשִׁסָּ֧היַעֲקֹ֛ב וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל לְבֹזְזִ֖ים הֲל֣וֹא יְהוָ֑ה ז֚וּ חָטָ֣אנוּ ל֔וֹ וְלֹֽא־אָב֤וּ בִדְרָכָיו֙ הָל֔וֹךְ וְלֹ֥א שָׁמְע֖וּ בְּתוֹרָתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Who gave to plunder Jacob, and Israel to despoilers? [Was it] not the LORD, whom we have sinned against him? And not they were willing in his ways to walk, and not they listened to his instruction.

en.L: Who gave Jacob to plunder and Israel to despoilers? [Was it] not {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q against whom we have sinned? \q And they were not willing to walk in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ways, \q and they did not listen to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} instruction.
en.B: Who gave Jacob up as spoil and Israel to raiders? Was it not {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q the one we sinned against? \q They refused to walk in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ways \q and would not heed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} instruction.
en.R: Who let robbers take everything from the people of Israel? \q It was {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and we sinned against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \q The people refused to live the way {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wanted. \q They did not obey {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} teaching.

es.L: ¿Quién entregó a Jacob al saqueo, y a Israel a los saqueadores? ¿No [fue] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q contra quien hemos pecado? \q Y no quisieron andar en {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} caminos, \q ni escucharon {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} instrucción.
es.B: ¿Quién entregó a Jacob como botín y a Israel a los saqueadores? ¿No fue {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q contra quien pecamos? \q Se negaron a andar en {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} caminos \q y no hicieron caso de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} instrucción.
es.R: ¿Quién dejó que los ladrones le quitaran todo al pueblo de Israel? \q Fue {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, y nosotros pecamos contra {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. \q El pueblo se negó a vivir como {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} quería. \q No obedecieron {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} enseñanza.

sw.L: Ni nani aliyemtoa Yakobo kuwa mateka, na Israeli kwa wanyang'anyi? Si {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q tuliyemtenda dhambi? \q Nao hawakutaka kuenenda katika njia {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}, \q wala hawakuyasikiliza mafundisho {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.B: Ni nani aliyemtoa Yakobo awe nyara na Israeli kwa wavamizi? Si {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q yule tuliyemkosea? \q Walikataa kutembea katika njia {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} \q na hawakuyatii mafundisho {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.R: Ni nani aliyewaacha wanyang'anyi wawachukulie watu wa Israeli kila kitu? \q Ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nasi tulimtenda dhambi. \q Watu walikataa kuishi jinsi {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alivyotaka. \q Hawakuyatii mafundisho {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.

decisions.choice: the LORD gave Israel to plunder: the exile as God's judgment
decisions.reason: The question answers itself: Israel's ruin was not the work of stronger gods but of the LORD, because of Israel's sin (Deuteronomy 28:47-52).

decisions.choice: we ... they: the speaker joins the confession, then describes Israel
decisions.reason: The prophet first includes himself ("we have sinned"), then speaks of the people ("they were not willing"), as in 6:5 and 64:4-5.

decisions.choice: to plunder: the reading of the margin (qere)
decisions.reason: The written text (ketiv) and the margin (qere) differ only in spelling; the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: the people of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable names Jacob and Israel together as the people of Israel and turns the second question into a statement.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁפֹּ֤ךְ עָלָיו֙ חֵמָ֣ה אַפּ֔וֹ וֶעֱז֖וּז מִלְחָמָ֑ה וַתְּלַהֲטֵ֤הוּ מִסָּבִיב֙ וְלֹ֣א יָדָ֔ע וַתִּבְעַר־בּ֖וֹ וְלֹא־יָשִׂ֥ים עַל־לֵֽב׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And he poured out on it [the] heat of his anger and [the] fierceness of battle; and it set it ablaze all around, and not it knew; and it burned in it, and not it set [it] on heart.

en.L: So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} poured out on him the heat of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger and the fierceness of battle; \q and it set him ablaze all around, but he did not know; \q and it burned him, but he did not lay [it] on [his] heart.
en.B: So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} poured out on them the heat of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger and the violence of battle. \q It set them ablaze on every side, yet they did not understand; \q it burned them, yet they gave it no thought.
en.R: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} poured out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger on them and sent war against them. \q It was like a fire burning all around them, but they still did not understand. \q It burned them, but they did not learn their lesson.

es.L: Así que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} derramó sobre él el ardor de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ira y la violencia de la guerra; \q y le prendió fuego por todos lados, pero no [lo] entendió; \q y lo quemó, pero no [lo] puso en [su] corazón.
es.B: Por eso {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} derramó sobre ellos el ardor de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ira y la furia de la guerra. \q Los envolvió en llamas por todos lados, y aun así no entendieron; \q los quemó, y no le dieron importancia.
es.R: Por eso {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} derramó {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ira sobre ellos y les envió la guerra. \q Fue como un fuego que ardía a su alrededor, pero aun así no entendieron. \q Los quemó, pero no aprendieron la lección.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo alimmwagia ukali wa hasira {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} na nguvu za vita; \q navyo vikamwasha pande zote, lakini yeye hakujua; \q na vikamchoma, lakini hakuliweka moyoni.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo aliwamwagia ukali wa hasira {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} na ghasia za vita. \q Viliwawashia moto pande zote, lakini hawakuelewa; \q viliwaunguza, lakini hawakulitafakari.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwamwagia hasira {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} na kuleta vita juu yao. \q Ilikuwa kama moto unaowaka pande zote, lakini bado hawakuelewa. \q Uliwaunguza, lakini hawakujifunza kitu.

decisions.choice: on him: Jacob, the people as one person
decisions.reason: The pronouns are singular and refer to Jacob/Israel in verse 24, the people pictured as one man.

decisions.choice: he did not lay it on his heart: he did not think about it or learn from it
decisions.reason: In Hebrew the heart is the seat of thought and will. The same phrase is used in 47:7 and 57:1.

decisions.choice: them
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the plural for the people, so the reader does not confuse the people with God; Literal keeps the singular.

decisions.choice: the LORD; It was like a fire
decisions.reason: Readable names the LORD as the one who poured out anger, and makes clear that the fire pictures the war.
